meta.title: x/tools/gopls/internal/analysis/modernize: minmax offers invalid fix when pattern appears beneath "else"
meta.fix_ref: golang/tools@81de76b22eab (gopls/internal/analysis/modernize: fix bug in minmax analyzer that incorrectly handles nested if-else)
meta.build_notes: Both built and run with go1.24.4 (golang.org/dl, under temp/lsp_servers/go-sdks; toolchain.json): the local go1.27 cannot build v0.18.1, go1.24.0 (current when v0.18.1 was tagged, 2025-02-24) cannot build v0.19.0 (its go.mod requires go >= 1.24.2), and go1.24.4 was the current Go release when v0.19.0 was tagged (2025-06-10). The fix merged 2025-05-29.
meta.notes: The minmax pass matched the inner 'if/else' of an else-if chain and replaced it by an assignment, leaving 'else f.focusedElement = min(...)', which is not valid syntax. The fix's regression test (nopeIfElseIf) expects no fix for an if/else-if/else chain.

settings_note: The modernize analyzer is on by default in both builds; the reporter ran the modernize command, which runs the same analyzer.

files.source: issue body, 'What did you do?' code block

files.note: a module around the file (the reporter used go 1.24.2 and gives no go.mod); go 1.24 (min/max need go1.21)

repro.steps: Open main.go. The minmax pass reports the if/else-if/else chain in SetFocus ('if/else statement can be modernized using min'). Apply its fix ('Replace if statement with min'). Reported (with the modernize command): '} else f.focusedElement = min(index, len(f.items) + len(f.buttons))', a syntax error ('else must be followed by if or statement block'). Probe: the edited text must have no parse error that the original did not have; no fix offered means absent (the fix stops offering it).
